title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-19
ranking_explanation: Selected the 10 highest daily star-gain values visible on the live GitHub daily Trending page at 2026-11-19 17:35 UTC; sorted descending by that signal.
global_caveat: Trending is a point-in-time sample and its gains, order, and total stars can change. The report preserves the values displayed on GitHub Trending at capture time; API corroboration may show small later star-count differences.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time (UTC): 2026-11-19 17:35 UTC. Scope: Daily. Date range: 2026-11-19 through 2026-11-19. Ranking basis: GitHub Trending daily star gains; selected 10 highest gains from the live daily page.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Coding-agent workflows and skills dominate today's high-growth repositories, led by Superpowers and Claude-BugHunter. The other strong thread is tooling that gives agents structured access to software and the web, especially CLI-Anything and Firecrawl.

sections.title: obra/superpowers
sections.description: An agentic skills framework and software-development methodology for coding agents.
sections.content: A coding-agent methodology whose README describes a staged workflow from specification and design through implementation planning, TDD, and subagent-driven development.
sections.why_notable: It leads today's sampled daily gains; its README describes a staged workflow from specification and design through implementation planning, TDD, and subagent-driven development.
sections.unique_caveat: The repository API reported its latest push as 2026-11-03, despite its strong daily star gain.

sections.title: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter
sections.description: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and authorized red-team work.
sections.content: A security-focused skill bundle; its README describes vulnerability-focused skills, disclosed-report patterns, and reporting, scope, and evidence-hygiene practices.
sections.why_notable: The second-largest gain in this snapshot, with a first-party README describing vulnerability-focused skills, disclosed-report patterns, and reporting/scope-hygiene practices.
sections.unique_caveat: GitHub Trending's description says 82 skills, while the README captured during research says 83; the count appears inconsistent or in transition.

sections.title: mvanhorn/last30days-skill
sections.description: An agent skill that researches recent topics across social, video, community, and web sources.
sections.content: Its README describes parallel cross-platform information gathering and engagement-based ranking, with an agent synthesizing results into a brief.
sections.why_notable: Its README frames cross-platform search and engagement-based ranking as an agent workflow, bridging research and coding-agent ecosystems.

sections.title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything
sections.description: “Making ALL Software Agent-Native,” with a community CLI hub.
sections.content: The project aims to make existing software callable by agents through command-line harnesses, with a hub for browsing and installing community-built CLIs.
sections.why_notable: It channels strong momentum into making existing software callable by agents through reusable command-line harnesses and a browseable/installable hub.
sections.unique_caveat: The repository API reported its latest push as 2026-09-22; high star momentum here does not imply recent code activity.

sections.title: firecrawl/firecrawl
sections.description: Web search, scraping, and data access infrastructure for agents.
sections.content: Its README highlights search, scrape, crawl, document parsing, interaction, and agent/MCP access as parts of one web-data toolkit.
sections.why_notable: It is the leading web-data infrastructure signal in this sample; its README highlights search, scrape, crawl, interaction, and agent/MCP access.

sections.title: mjmirza/app-store-compliance
sections.description: A playbook and pre-submission guard for app-store requirements.
sections.content: A policy and release-checklist resource that also advertises a skill for AI coding agents.
sections.why_notable: It packages policy and release-checklist knowledge into a tool that can also be used by AI coding agents.

sections.title: XiaoYouChR/Ghost-Downloader-3
sections.content: GitHub Trending describes it as a general-purpose downloader; its daily gain makes it a high-growth end-user utility in an otherwise agent-heavy sample.
sections.why_notable: It is a high-growth end-user utility, a counterpoint to the otherwise agent-heavy sample.

sections.title: cursor/plugins
sections.description: Cursor's plugin specification and official plugins.
sections.content: An official plugin catalog whose daily gain signals interest in extensible editor-agent integrations.
sections.why_notable: The official catalog's daily gain is a direct signal of demand for extensible editor-agent integrations.

sections.title: cathrynlavery/diagram-design
sections.description: Editorial diagram patterns for coding-agent tools, implemented with HTML and SVG.
sections.content: A focused diagram-design toolkit aimed at coding-agent environments, representing a creative-workflow niche in today's sample.
sections.why_notable: Its focused design-tooling approach shows a practical creative-workflow niche alongside agent infrastructure.

sections.title: google-labs-code/stitch-skills
sections.description: Agent Skills for working with Google's Stitch MCP server.
sections.content: A library of Agent Skills for a design tool's MCP server, with stated compatibility across several coding-agent hosts.
sections.why_notable: It connects an agent-skills format to a design tool and explicitly targets compatibility across multiple coding-agent hosts.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Coding-agent skills and workflows: Superpowers, Claude-BugHunter, last30days-skill, cursor/plugins, app-store-compliance, and stitch-skills package procedures, integrations, research, or domain knowledge for agent environments. Agent access to software and information: CLI-Anything offers command-line harnesses, Firecrawl provides web-data capabilities, and last30days-skill aggregates research sources. Design workflows and end-user utilities remain in the mix through diagram-design, stitch-skills, and Ghost-Downloader-3. Languages in the ten selected repositories: Python 4, TypeScript 3, Shell 2, HTML 1.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's strongest signal is that agent tooling is moving from prompt collections toward repeatable workflows, specialized skills, and practical interfaces to software and information sources. The gains are not confined to new agent frameworks: editor ecosystems, security workflows, web-data infrastructure, and conventional utilities are also attracting substantial attention.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary source: GitHub Trending daily page, https://github.com/trending?since=daily, read 2026-11-19 at 17:35 UTC. Corroboration: GitHub Search API queries for the five narration-priority repositories and GitHub REST repository plus default-branch commit endpoints for all ten. Daily gains and total stars preserve the Trending-page snapshot; API confirmed repository metadata and current commit SHAs. First-party README content was reviewed for the five narration-priority projects. Ranking is descending daily star gains. No prior-window comparison was used.
